summary.headline: Interarch Q2 FY27 revenue rose 2.9% to INR505 crores with EBITDA flat at INR41.7 crores; management reiterates FY27 revenue guidance of INR2,150-2,200 crores.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR505 crores versus INR491 crores in Q2 FY26, with EBITDA of INR41.7 crores (8.3% margin vs 8.5%) and PAT of INR30.7 crores versus INR32.3 crores, hit by higher depreciation from new Gujarat and Andhra Pradesh plants and lower interest income. H1 FY27 revenue grew 10.7% to about INR1,0XX crores (figure garbled in transcript) with H1 EBITDA margin at 8.4%. Management said the H2 execution pick-up is expected, the residual order book is above INR2,000 crores, and it is shifting new orders almost entirely to variable steel pricing amid record steel prices. Management also highlighted heavy structure (HSS) and export verticals that carry higher upfront opex before revenue.

segments.name: Pre-engineered buildings (PEB)
segments.commentary: Core business; over 72% of customers are repeat buyers for heavy steel structures and exports per management. Standard PEB pieces are mostly under 5 tons, and order book is about 9 months of production.

segments.name: Heavy steel structures (HSS)
segments.commentary: Plant capacity currently 25,000 tons, rising to about 75,000-80,000 tons by end of next year; commenced operations on 24 September 2026. About INR300-350 crores of the INR2,000 crore order book (15-20%) is HSS, covering data centres, a hospital, a hotel, a Delhi commercial building and process buildings; management says the lines are fully loaded.

segments.name: Exports / OWSJ JV
segments.commentary: Open Web Steel Joists JV with ER Steel Canada for North America; initial funding INR50 crores as planned. Export orders expected to be executed mainly in Q3 and Q4; African projects under way. Management expects INR100-200 crores of export revenue in two to three years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR2,150-2,200 crores reiterated; implies roughly INR600 crores per quarter in Q3 and Q4 per the analyst's arithmetic. Management said H1 is the guide and H2 is typically larger.
Management expects H2 turnover of about INR1,200 crores (versus about INR1,000 crores in H1 as stated); margins to improve in H2 but not to exceed the 9-9.5% level.
FY27 margins not expected to see major improvement; FY28 margin improvement expected as Gujarat, HSS and exports ramp up.

Medium-term target: 10-12% EBITDA margin on orders over the next 12 months and about 11-12% within two years; long-term aspiration above 14-15%. Earlier guidance of 9.5-10% EBITDA by FY28 referenced by analyst.

Capacity: about 80,000 tons available in FY28 from Gujarat and HSS plants; target about 100,000 tons usable additional capacity by March 2028 and a further 100,000 tons by mid-2029, taking total to about 400,000 tons.
capex_capacity: Gujarat (both phases) and Andhra Pradesh Phase 1 are operational; each PEB plant adds about 40,000 tons of capacity.

Heavy structure plant at 25,000 tons currently, commissioned 24 September 2026; target 75,000-80,000 tons by end of next year. HSS Phase 2 expected to finish around March-April 2027, Phase 3 around November-December 2027.
Company has spent about INR250 crores on capex to date, funded from internal resources and working capital limits, against an IPO raise of INR180 crores.
Management aims for order book intake of INR200-220 crores per month over the next 12 months, matching capacity; current book is about nine months of production.
QIP: formalities completed; timing left to advisers Ambit, with launch possible at 72-hour notice.
demand_pricing: Residual order book above INR2,000 crores as of 31 October 2026; about 70-75% executes within 9-10 months, with two or three longer orders at 12-16 months; blended period 10-11 months.

Pricing mix: about 35-40% variable price (full steel pass-through) and about 60% fixed price, booked at current or near-current prices. Management says no fixed-price orders have been taken in the last two to three months and policy is now variable-only.
Order pipeline is about five to six times monthly order throughput, which is about INR600-700 crores per quarter.

Steel prices are at a record high, reportedly the highest since 2022, with analyst noting an 18-20% year-on-year increase; management said prices rose during the monsoon and supply has been disrupted.
Management cites competition and steel price swings as having compressed margins; it says it is willing to lose orders rather than accept fixed pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What is HSS capacity utilisation, ramp-up, and EBITDA per ton / margin for heavy structures?
qa_highlights.answer: HSS pieces are over 5 tons (up to 20-25 tons); steel prices are fully passed through and payment is due before dispatch. Management expects similar margins but higher net margin as overheads are leveraged; the plant is currently 25,000 tons and will reach 75,000-80,000 tons by end of next year.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days rose from 66 to 86 in H1; is this the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Manish Garg attributed it to longer order-to-cash cycles on larger orders, steel stocking during supply disruption, and new Gujarat and HSS plants. Net working capital is about 44 days after customer advances; there is room to improve receivables and inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue guidance of INR2,150-2,200 crores still achievable given H1 growth of around 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 is the better guide because H2 typically carries more clearances, and the company remains confident in executing the INR2,150-2,200 crore plan with no change.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall to 8.3% and how will it reach the FY28 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Export and new-vertical opex is incurred before revenue. Management cited steel price spikes and oil and freight costs, offset by price increases to customers. It expects margin improvement from operational leverage, HSS, exports and steel prices stabilising, with the target expected to clear in FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: Why are erection and installation charges up to 11% of revenue from 9% a year ago?
qa_highlights.answer: Each job is lump-sum costed, and erection and freight are pass-through items charged to customers; the rise reflects job mix (larger and remote jobs), not a margin cost.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY27 margins evolve and what drove the steel price impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects no major FY27 margin improvement; H2 margins should improve but stay around 9-9.5%. Orders executed in Q3-Q4 were booked at higher steel prices in Q1-Q2 and October steel prices rose again, so Q3 may see a margin hit.

qa_highlights.question: Why shift to variable pricing and what is the capacity roadmap?
qa_highlights.answer: Variable pricing shifts steel price risk to customers and customers also prefer it at current record prices. Capacity: about 40,000 tons per PEB plant; about 80,000 tons from Gujarat and HSS in FY28, with a target of 100,000 tons usable by March 2028 and a further 100,000 tons by mid-2029, reaching about 400,000 tons.

risks_watch: Steel price volatility at record highs and supply disruption; October steel prices rose again, so Q3 margins could be hit before stabilising.
Margin compression: EBITDA margin 8.3% versus the 9.5-10% FY28 target, with new-vertical opex running ahead of revenue.
Working capital days rose from 66 to 86 in H1; receivables and inventory need to normalise.
Execution risk in H2: FY27 revenue needs about INR600 crores per quarter; HSS Phase 2 and 3 timelines depend on schedule.
Export and JV ramp-up (OWSJ with ER Steel Canada) and the QIP timing, both still undefined.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term outlook and order book, but candid that margins are under pressure from steel prices and new-vertical costs. Management repeatedly deflected quarter-on-quarter margin questions to a full-year view. Some answers were discursive and figures (H1 absolutes, PAT) were garbled in the transcript.
key_quotes: So, we are very confident that the capacity exists, the order book we have and the clearances we have.

So, we want to protect ourselves from any steel price increase or decrease, wherever we can get a better margin, and where the customer is top quality, and it gives us the ability to do new kinds of buildings.
Our second-quarter results have been broadly in line with the same quarter last year.
But right now our policy is to take only variable pricing.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance of INR2,150-2,200 crores reiterated (about 8% growth implied on the midpoint, using ~INR1,000 crores H1 and ~INR1,200 crores H2), backed by a residual order book above INR2,000 crores and HSS plant commissioned 24 Sept 2026, though the H2 ramp implies roughly INR600 crores per quarter versus INR505 crores in Q2, and the H1 absolute figure was garbled in the transcript.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin 8.3% vs 8.5% a year ago; management sees H2 FY27 at only about 9-9.5% and Q3 may take a steel-price hit, with 11-12% targeted only within two years, so expansion is conditional on HSS, exports and steel prices stabilising.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: HSS plant of 25,000 t commissioned 24 Sept 2026 and rising to 75,000-80,000 t by end of next year; HSS Phase 2 around Mar-Apr 2027 and Phase 3 around Nov-Dec 2027; about 100,000 t more targeted by March 2028 (about INR250 crore capex spent to date).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 volume was 41,600 t, up only 1% YoY, but FY27 revenue guidance of INR2,150-2,200 crore needs about INR600 crore per quarter in Q3-Q4 versus INR505 crore in Q2, and the residual order book is above INR2,000 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management has already planned about 100,000 t more by March 2028 and a further 100,000 t by mid-2029, and a QIP is formally ready to launch on 72-hour notice, so further capex is likely to be announced or funded.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance of INR2,150-2,200 crore was only reiterated, and H1 growth of about 10.7% needs a steep H2 step-up, so an upgrade is not on the table; margin guidance was in fact trimmed to 9-9.5% for H2.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Steel prices rose again in October and Q3 margins may take a hit; H2 revenue needs about INR1,200 crore versus about INR1,000 crore in H1, and the transcript garbled the H1 absolute, so the execution risk is real.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Export orders (OWSJ JV with ER Steel Canada, African projects) are to be executed mainly in Q3-Q4 FY27, with INR100-200 crore of export revenue expected in two to three years; HSS is already in production.

rows.label: Working capital days normalisation
rows.why: Working capital days rose from 66 to 86 in H1 with net working capital at 44 days after advances, and management sees room to improve receivables and inventory.

rows.label: Order book intake of INR200-220 crore per month
rows.why: Order pipeline is about 5-6 times monthly throughput of INR600-700 crore a quarter, and the residual order book is above INR2,000 crore with about 9 months of production cover.

rows.label: Shift to variable steel pricing
rows.why: About 35-40% of the book is already variable-priced, no fixed-price orders have been taken in the last 2-3 months, and management is willing to lose orders rather than accept fixed pricing.

tone.note: Management was confident on the order book, the HSS ramp and the FY27 revenue guide, but cautious on margins under record steel prices and new-vertical opex, and it deflected quarter-on-quarter margin questions; analysts pushed on H2 revenue achievability, the working capital jump from 66 to 86 days
